tier1.text: Each mylohyoid helps press the tongue to the top of the mouth. Each mylohyoid also lifts the hyoid bone, a small U-shaped bone in the upper neck. The mylohyoid muscles lie beneath the floor of the mouth. Each mylohyoid runs from the mandible, or lower jaw, to the hyoid bone.

quotes.quote: The horseshoe-shaped part of the oral cavity bounded superiorly by the ventral surface of the tongue, inferiorly by the mylohyoid muscle, anterolaterally by the gingival surfaces of the mandible, and posteriorly by the anterior tonsillar pillar.

quotes.quote: One of the suprahyoid muscles located superior to the anterior belly of the digastric muscle that has its origin on the mandible, its insertion on the hyoid bone, and functions to elevate the hyoid, the tongue, and the floor of the mouth.
quotes.citation: NCI Thesaurus (NCIt), National Cancer Institute, https://ncithesaurus.nci.nih.gov
